text: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $x\mathrm{d}y=\left (\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}+y\right )\mathrm{d}x,x>0$, intersect the line $x=1$ at $y=0$ and the line $x=2$ at $y=α$. Then the value of $α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{xdy-ydx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}=dx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}}{x}+\frac{y}{x}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{1+\frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}}+\frac{y}{x}$

Let $\frac{y}{x}=v$

$\Rightarrow v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\sqrt{1+v^{2}}+v$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{\sqrt{1+v^{2}}}=\frac{dx}{x}$

OR $\ln \left (v+\sqrt{1+v^{2}}\right )=\ln x+C$

at $x=1,y=0$

$\Rightarrow C=0$

$\frac{y}{x}+\sqrt{1+\frac{y^{2}}{x^{2}}}=x$

At $x=2$,

$\frac{y}{2}+\sqrt{1+\frac{y^{2}}{4}}=2$

$\Rightarrow 1+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=4+\frac{y^{2}}{4}-2y$

OR $y=\frac{3}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: For $α\in 𝐍$, consider a relation $\mathrm{R}$ on $𝐍$ given by $\mathrm{R}=\{(x,y):3x+αy$ is a multiple of 7$\}$. The relation $R$ is an equivalence relation if and only if :
options: 4 is the remainder when $α$ is divided by 10
4 is the remainder when $α$ is divided by 7
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For R to be reflexive, $(x,x)\in R$ for every $x\in 𝐍$, i.e. $(3+α)x$ is a multiple of $7$ for all $x$. Taking $x=1$, $3+α\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}7)$, so $α\equiv 4(\mathrm{mod}7)$.

Conversely, let $α=7m+4$. Then $3x+αy=3x+4y+7my$, so $(x,y)\in R⟺3x+4y\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}7)$.

Since $4y\equiv -3y(\mathrm{mod}7)$, this condition is $3(x-y)\equiv 0(\mathrm{mod}7)$, and as $3$ is coprime to $7$, $(x,y)\in R⟺x\equiv y(\mathrm{mod}7)$.

Congruence modulo $7$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so R is an equivalence relation exactly when $α$ leaves remainder $4$ on division by $7$.

$α=14$ satisfies (A) and (C) but leaves remainder $0$ on division by $7$, so those conditions do not give an equivalence relation.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text:
If $y=y(x),x\in (0,π/2)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation 

$\left (\sin ^{2}2x\right )\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (8\sin ^{2}2x+2\sin 4x\right )y=2\mathrm{e}^{-4x}(2\sin 2x+\cos 2x)$, 

with $y(π/4)=\mathrm{e}^{-π}$, then $y(π/6)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(\sin ^{2}2x)\frac{dy}{dx}+(8\sin ^{2}2x+2\sin 4x)y$

$=2e^{-4x}(2\sin 2x+\cos 2x)$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+(8+4\cot 2x)y=2e^{-4x}\left (\frac{2\sin 2x+\cos 2x}{\sin ^{2}2x}\right )$

Integrating factor

$(I.F.)=e^{\int (8+4\cot 2x)dx}$

$=e^{8x+2\ln \sin 2x}$

Solution of differential equation

$y.e^{8x+2\ln \sin 2x}$

$=\int 2e^{(4x+2\ln \sin 2x)}\frac{(2\sin 2x+\cos 2x)}{\sin ^{2}2x}dx$

$=2\int e^{4x}(2\sin 2x+\cos 2x)dx$

$y.e^{8x+2\ln \sin 2x}=e^{4x}\sin 2x+c$

$y\left (\frac{π}{4}\right )=e^{-π}$

$e^{-π}.\qquad e^{2π}=e^{π}+c\Rightarrow c=0$

$y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )=\frac{e^{\dfrac{2π}{3}}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{e^{\left (\dfrac{4π}{3}+2\ln \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right )}}$

$=e^{\frac{-2π}{3}}.\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: Let $C$ be the centre of the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-x+2y=\frac{11}{4}$ and $P$ be a point on the circle. A line passes through the point $\mathrm{C}$, makes an angle of $\frac{π}{4}$ with the line $\mathrm{CP}$ and intersects the circle at the points $Q$ and $R$. Then the area of the triangle $PQR$ (in unit ${}^{2}$ ) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-x+2y-\dfrac{11}{4}=0$ has centre $C\left (\dfrac{1}{2},-1\right )$ and radius

$r=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+1+\frac{11}{4}}=2.$

The line through $C$ meets the circle at the ends of a diameter, so $QR=2r=4$.

$P$ is on the circle with $CP=2$, and $CP$ makes an angle $\dfrac{π}{4}$ with $QR$, so the perpendicular distance of $P$ from $QR$ is

$h=CP\sin \frac{π}{4}=2\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}.$

$\text{Area of}△PQR=\frac{1}{2}\times QR\times h=\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times \sqrt{2}=2\sqrt{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: Let $α,β$ and $γ$ be three positive real numbers. Let $f(x)=αx^{5}+βx^{3}+γx,x\in 𝐑$ and $g:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be such that $g(f(x))=x$ for all $x\in 𝐑$. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f\left (g\left (\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}f(a_{i})\right )\right )$

$\frac{a_{1}+a_{2}+a_{3}+......+a_{n}}{n}=0$

$\therefore$ First and last term, second and second last and so on are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign.

$f(x)=αx^{5}+βx^{3}+γx$

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}f(a_{i})=α\left (a_{1}^{5}+a_{2}^{5}+a_{3}^{5}+.....+a_{n}^{5}\right )+β\left (a_{1}^{3}+a_{2}^{3}+....+a_{n}^{3}\right )+γ(a_{1}+a_{2}+....+a_{n})$

$=0$

$\therefore$ $f\left (g\left (\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}f(a_{i})\right )\right )=\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits _{i=1}^{n}f(a_{i})=0$

text: Let $S$ be the set of all passwords which are six to eight characters long, where each character is either an alphabet from $\{A,B,C,D,E\}$ or a number from $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ with the repetition of characters allowed. If the number of passwords in $S$ whose at least one character is a number from $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ is $α\times 5^{6}$, then $α$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If password is 6 character long, then

Total number of ways having atleast one number $=10^{6}-5^{6}$

Similarly, if 7 character long $=10^{7}-5^{7}$

and if 8-character long $=10^{8}-5^{8}$

Number of password $=(10^{6}+10^{7}+10^{8})-(5^{6}+5^{7}+5^{8})$

$=5^{6}(2^{6}+5.2^{7}+25.2^{8}-1-5-25)$

$=5^{6}(64+640+6400-31)$

$=7073\times 5^{6}$

$\therefore$ $α=7073$.

text: Let $\mathrm{P}(-2,-1,1)$ and $\mathrm{Q}\left (\frac{56}{17},\frac{43}{17},\frac{111}{17}\right )$ be the vertices of the rhombus PRQS. If the direction ratios of the diagonal RS are $α,-1,β$, where both $α$ and $β$ are integers of minimum absolute values, then $α^{2}+β^{2}$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the rhombus $PRQS$ the vertices are taken in the order $P,R,Q,S$, so $PQ$ and $RS$ are its diagonals, and the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular.


[IMG]

Direction ratios of $PQ$: $\left (\dfrac{56}{17}+2,\dfrac{43}{17}+1,\dfrac{111}{17}-1\right )=\left (\dfrac{90}{17},\dfrac{60}{17},\dfrac{94}{17}\right )$, proportional to $(45,30,47)$.

Since $RS⟂PQ$:

$45α+30(-1)+47β=0\Rightarrow 45α+47β=30$

Then $47β=15(2-3α)$, and since 47 and 15 have no common factor, $β=15k$ for an integer $k$. Substituting, $3α+47k=2$, so $α=\dfrac{2-47k}{3}$, an integer only for $k=1,-2,4,\ldots$

$k=1$ gives $(α,β)=(-15,15)$, $k=-2$ gives $(32,-30)$ and $k=4$ gives $(-62,60)$; other values of $k$ give larger values still, so $(α,β)=(-15,15)$.

$α^{2}+β^{2}=225+225=450$

Hence, the answer is 450.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{15x^{3}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}+\sqrt{(1+x^{2})^{3}}}}\mathrm{d}x=α\sqrt{2}+β\sqrt{3}$, where $α,β$ are integers, then $α+β$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $x=\tan θ\Rightarrow dx=\sec ^{2}θdθ$

$\Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{15\tan ^{3}θ.\sec ^{2}θdθ}{\sqrt{1+\tan ^{2}θ+\sqrt{\sec ^{6}θ}}}$

$\Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{15\tan ^{2}θ\sec ^{2}θdθ}{\sec θ\sqrt{1+\sec θ}}$

$\Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{3}}\frac{15(\sec ^{2}θ-1)\sec θ\tan θdθ}{\left (\sqrt{1+\sec θ}\right )}$

Now put $1+\sec θ=t^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \sec θ\tan θdθ=2tdt$

$\Rightarrow I=\int\limits _{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{15\left ((t^{2}-1)^{2}-1\right )2tdt}{t}$

$\Rightarrow I=30\int\limits _{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}(t^{4}-2t^{2}+1-1)dt$

$\Rightarrow I=30\int\limits _{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}}(t^{4}-2t^{2})dt$

$\Rightarrow I=30\left (\frac{t^{5}}{5}-\frac{2t^{3}}{3}\right )\left |_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} \right.$

$=30\left [\left (\frac{9}{5}\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}\right )-\left (\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{5}-\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\right )\right ]$

$=\left (54\sqrt{3}-60\sqrt{3}\right )-\left (24\sqrt{2}-40\sqrt{2}\right )$

$=16\sqrt{2}-6\sqrt{3}$

$\therefore$ $α=16$ and $β=-6$

$α+β=10.$

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & α \end{array}\right ]$ and $B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ],α,β\in 𝐑$. Let $α_{1}$ be the value of $α$ which satisfies $(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})^{2}=\mathrm{A}^{2}+\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$ and $α_{2}$ be the value of $α$ which satisfies $(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B})^{2}=\mathrm{B}^{2}$. Then $|α_{1}-α_{2}|$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(A+B)^{2}=A^{2}+B^{2}+AB+BA$

$=A^{2}+\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $B^{2}+AB+BA=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$ ..... (1)

$AB=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & α \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β-1 & 1 \\ α+2β & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

$BA=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & α \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β+2 & α-β \\ 1 & -1 \end{array}\right ]$

$B^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} β & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} β^{2}+1 & β \\ β & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

By (1) we get

$\left [\begin{array}{ll} β^{2}+2β+2 & α+1 \\ α+3β+1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

$\therefore$ $α=1β=0\Rightarrow α_{1}=1$

Similarly if $A^{2}+AB+BA=0$ then

$\left (A^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & α \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & α \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} -1 & -1-α \\ 2+2α & α^{2}-2 \end{array}\right ]\right )$

$\left [\begin{array}{ll} 2β & α-β+1-1-α \\ α+2β+1+2+2α & α^{2}-2+1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow β=0$ and $α=-1\Rightarrow α_{2}=-1$

$\therefore$ $|α_{1}-α_{2}|=|2|=2.$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift

text: For $\mathrm{p},\mathrm{q}\in 𝐑$, consider the real valued function $f(x)=(x-\mathrm{p})^{2}-\mathrm{q},x\in 𝐑$ and $\mathrm{q}>0$. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $x+2\cos x=a$

$x+2=b$

as $x\to 0$, $a\to 2$ and $b\to 2$

$\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{a^{3}+2a^{2}+3\sin a}{b^{3}+2b^{2}+3\sin b}\right )^{\frac{100}{x}}$

$=e^{\lim _{x\to 0}.\frac{100}{x}.\frac{(a3-b3)+2(a2-b2)+3(\sin a-\sin b)}{b3+2b2+3\sin b}}$

$\because$ $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{a-b}{x}=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{2(\cos x-1)}{x}=0$

$=e^{0}$

$=1$
